review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer questioned the effectiveness of checking the flags of a given item, citing potential false negatives if squota is not used or if the size is small, and suggested an alternative approach to identify qgroup status items missing enable_gen

Reviewer Qu Wenruo pointed out that the tree-checker's principle is to verify every member of a variable-sized structure, and specifically noted that checking flags like RESCAN/INCONSISTENT may not be necessary for regular qgroups since it's valid for them to not have these flags set. However, he suggested adding a check in simple mode to ensure the RESCAN flag is not set.
review_comments.raw_body:
Yes, the reason is correct.

For those still running qgroups and have never disabled it (which I 
believe they are minority now), their qgroup status items will stay 
without the enable_gen member.

---

This is the common practice for tree-checker, remember that tree-checker 
is the "2nd best memory tester" to catch weird problems, not only from 
btrfs, but also bad hardware.

So the principle is not "this should not happen so we don't need to 
check" but "every member should be verified when possible".

And this is part of the common path for any variable sized structure, we 
need to make sure the added member is not beyond the item boundary.


Finally for the "why not look for normal ones missing rescan or flags or 
whatever" part, that's because for regular qgroups, it's completely 
valid to not have RESCAN/INCONSISTENT flag set, so we do not need to 
check that.

But this inspired me that, for simple mode we should not have RESCAN 
flag set.
I'll add this check into the next version.

Thanks for the review,
Qu

patches_acked.subject: Re: [PATCH] btrfs: remove runtime tweakable feature sysfs interface
patches_acked.patch_summary: This patch removes the sysfs interface for runtime tweakable features in Btrfs, which allows certain behaviors to be dynamically adjusted without using ioctl or mount options. The removal is motivated by the fact that some features are not at whole filesystem granularity and the generic features mechanism no longer makes sense. This change simplifies the code and aligns with a desire to converge on using only ioctl for runtime feature setting.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Qu Wenruo expressed no issues with the current sysfs interfaces, finding them more straightforward and less prone to compatibility problems compared to mount options, but noted that there is a potential race condition with mount/unmount operations.

Reviewer noted that the original assumption about features being enabled halfway was overly optimistic, and suggested that enabling work should be pushed into user-space programs rather than the kernel itself.
review_comments.raw_body:
Personally speaking I have no problem with the current sysfs interfaces 
at all.

It's more straightforward, less compatibility problems compared to mount 
options.

The only down side is the race with mount/unmount, but it's not a big 
deal as long as we're only modifying a single in-memory flag/value.

---

I think the features interface itself is totally fine, just we were a 
little too optimistic on the features that can be enabled halfway.

Nowadays if we want to introduce some new features, we will be more 
cautious and push most of the enabling work into progs other than the 
kernel itself, and may not choose to allowing mixed old and new structures.

Thanks for the review,
Qu

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 01/14] NFSD: cap the number of listeners accepted in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the number of listeners accepted in the listener_set function to prevent a userland request from spinning indefinitely due to a nested loop that runs under sv_lock with bottom halves disabled. The limit is set at NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024) entries, which is far above any realistic configuration. This change does not cap the number of existing listeners but rather prevents new requests from exceeding this threshold. The patch also adds a check in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners to reject oversized listener lists before taking any locks.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 02/14] NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a validation check for the transport name in the listener_set function of NFSD before service creation. It ensures that only supported transport names (tcp, udp, and rdma) are accepted to prevent unknown names from triggering a request_module upcall under nfsd_mutex. The check is performed in the nfsd_nl_validate_listeners function, which runs before taking the nfsd_mutex lock. If an unsupported name is detected, it returns an error with a descriptive message indicating the offending attribute.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 03/14] SUNRPC: keep the first error in svc_register()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register() function in the SUNRPC module to keep track of the first error encountered during RPC program registration, rather than overwriting it with subsequent errors. This ensures that an earlier failure is not erased by a later success or failure. The fix addresses a problem introduced by a previous patch that allowed further customization of RPC program registration.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 04/14] SUNRPC: bound the local rpcbind client timeout to 1s
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the timeout for local rpcbind client connections to 1 second. The previous default timeouts of 10 seconds and 60 seconds were causing stalls in NFS server operations, leading to hung-task watchdog warnings. By bounding the timeout to a single attempt of 1 second, the patch reduces the duration of these stalls, but does not eliminate them entirely. A more comprehensive fix would involve making the registration process asynchronous. The change affects the kernel's local rpcbind client, which communicates with the local rpcbind service over loopback or AF_LOCAL sockets.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 05/14] NFSD: report listener creation failures through extack
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) code to report listener creation failures through extack, providing more detailed error information to userland. Specifically, it records the attribute and transport name of the entry that failed and reports both after the loop, allowing for more precise identification of the issue. This change addresses a limitation where only generic error messages were provided, making it harder to diagnose specific problems.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 06/14] SUNRPC: report local rpcbind calls that get no answer
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to report local rpcbind calls that receive no answer, allowing callers to distinguish between failures due to a non-responsive rpcbind and other types of errors. The patch introduces new error codes to categorize rpcbind call failures into three groups: answered (with a specific set of error codes), never sent (with a different set of error codes), and no answer (all remaining error codes). A count of unanswered rpcbind calls is also maintained in the serv structure, which will be used by later patches to adjust behavior based on hard rpcbind failures.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 07/14] SUNRPC: stop svc_register() once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register function in the SUNRPC module to stop registering programs and versions when the local rpcbind client times out, rather than continuing to try other programs and versions. This change is made to prevent unnecessary delays and wasted time when a program's call to the local rpcbind times out. The approach taken is to add a new condition that breaks out of the loop if no answer was received from the rpcbind client.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 08/14] SUNRPC: stop the svc_unregister() sweep once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_unregister() function to stop sweeping for stale rpcbind entries once it receives no answer from rpcbind. This is done to prevent unnecessary timeouts and improve performance when a local rpcbind never replies. The change affects how nfsd services handle listener setup and cleanup, reducing the number of timeouts incurred due to non-responsive rpcbind servers.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 09/14] SUNRPC: stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering. The original behavior caused multiple timeouts for each listener, which was unnecessary and inefficient. When rpcbind fails to respond, the patch clears a flag on remaining transport listeners, preventing further timeouts.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 10/14] NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in the NFSD code by stopping registration with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set. The current implementation calls svc_xprt_create_from_sa() for each requested listener, which can lead to multiple registrations with rpcbind and subsequent timeouts. To mitigate this, the patch reads the rpcb_failure_count before creating listeners and skips registering with rpcbind if it has failed previously. This approach reduces the likelihood of prolonged lock contention on nfsd_mutex.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 11/14] selftests/nfsd: exercise listener_set request validation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds regression tests for the NFSD_CMD_LISTENER_SET checks in the NFS server (NFSD) code. The tests cover various invalid listener set requests, including bad transport names, missing addresses, and malformed entries. The tests use a stub to simulate the creation of an NFS service and run in their own network namespace. The patch also updates the MAINTAINERS file and adds a new directory for the NFSD selftests.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 12/14] selftests/nfsd: add a per-netns rpcbind stub and the listener round-trips
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a per-netns rpcbind stub to the selftests/nfsd suite, allowing tests to run within their own network namespace. The stub serves as a minimal responder that answers RPCBVERS_4 and RPCBVERS_2 requests, counts accepted connections and received calls, and shares mode information with the test. With this stub in place, additional tests are added to cover various scenarios, including listener creation, addition, removal, and round-trips for TCP, UDP, and IPv6 listeners. The patch also includes fixes for netlink socket configuration and teardown procedures to prevent namespace leaks.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 13/14] selftests/nfsd: check that listener_set asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds tests to the selftests/nfsd module to ensure that the listener_set request only asks rpcbind once. The patch introduces new constants and procedures, including RPCB_STUB_SILENT, which silences a call without sending an answer, and version_set_only(), which makes the server v4-only by clearing all versions before reading the request. The tests cover various scenarios, including stopping a listener_set request from registering after rpcbind stops answering, checking that unregistration is handled correctly, and verifying that multiple listeners are not registered unnecessarily.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 14/14] selftests/nfsd: check that listener removal asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a test case to the NFS daemon selftest suite to verify that removing a listener from the RPC bind service only results in one call to rpcbind, even if multiple listeners are removed at once. The test creates a stub RPC bind service and registers three listeners with it, then removes them one by one while monitoring the number of calls made to rpcbind. It checks that the second and third removals do not result in additional calls to rpcbind, ensuring that the listener removal process is efficient and does not incur unnecessary overhead.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to harden the netlink listener set interface in the NFS daemon (nfsd) and SunRPC code by introducing early error handling, reducing unnecessary RPC calls, and improving timeout handling. The goal is to prevent hangs and improve overall performance.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton
review_comments.summary: The reviewer suggested that the patches are a good start, but some of the changes may not be necessary. They asked for more information about the performance benefits and whether the changes can be made more incremental.
review_comments.raw_body:
nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() matches each requested listener against the
existing set. The nested loop that does this is O(N * M), where N is the
requested count and M is the existing count. The loop runs under sv_lock
with bottom halves disabled. A userland request with a very large listener
list can therefore spin in atomic context for a long time.

Reject a request that carries more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024)
entries. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), before the code
takes any lock. The limit is far above any realistic configuration.

This patch does not cap M. Only the message size bounded N; real sockets
bound M. A listener_set result set is the requested set, so that path also
holds M at the cap, but __write_ports_addxprt() adds two listeners per call
and removes none, so repeated calls can push M past it. The worst case
under sv_lock is therefore 1024 * M, plus 1024 nla_parse_nested() calls.
Both interfaces require CAP_NET_ADMIN.

Fixes: 16a471177496 ("NFSD: add listener-{set,get} netlink command")
Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c | 16 +++++++++++-----
 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
index 5331b89c4281..b6f4d66f612a 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
@@ -1995,21 +1995,22 @@ int nfsd_nl_version_get_doit(struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info)
 	return err;
 }
 
+/* Upper bound on the number of listeners a single request may carry. */
+#define NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX	1024
+
 /**
  * nfsd_nl_validate_listeners - sanity-check the listener list from userland
  * @info: netlink metadata and command arguments
  *
- * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that each entry
- * is well-formed: it parses against the policy, carries both an address and
- * a transport name, and the address is long enough for its family. Doing
- * this up front lets the callers below assume every entry is valid and
- * guarantees we make no changes when the request is malformed.
+ * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that the list is
+ * not oversized and that each entry is well-formed.
  *
  * Return: 0 if every entry is valid, or a negative errno otherwise.
  */
 static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 {
 	const struct nlattr *attr;
+	unsigned int count = 0;
 	int rem;
 
 	nlmsg_for_each_attr_type(attr, NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR, info->nlhdr,
@@ -2018,6 +2019,11 @@ static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 		struct sockaddr *sa;
 		int err;
 
+		if (++count > NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX) {
+			NL_SET_ERR_MSG(info->extack, "too many listeners");
+			return -E2BIG;
+		}
+
 		err = nla_parse_nested(tb, NFSD_A_SOCK_MAX, attr,
 				       nfsd_sock_nl_policy, info->extack);
 		if (err < 0)

--

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 1/7] mm/memcontrol: flatten try_charge_memcg control flow
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the try_charge_memcg function in the Linux kernel's memory control module to simplify its control flow by separating the logic for memsw and memory page counters into distinct paths.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 2/7] mm/page_counter: report the number of pages charged
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds an optional parameter to the page_counter_try_charge function, which returns the number of pages actually charged to the hierarchy when successful. This change is made to accommodate a future update in the series where stock can be pushed down from the memcg level to the page_counter level, potentially changing how charges are accounted for. The new parameter is added to all callsites and is used by only one user (try_charge_memcg) to track the hierarchy size growth.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 3/7] mm/page_counter: introduce per-page_counter stock
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces per-page_counter stock to improve the efficiency of memcg charge and limit checks. The current implementation uses per-cpu stocks, which can lead to expensive hierarchy walks and inefficient cache management. By pushing stock caches down to the page_counter level, each counter is responsible for its own charge, addressing issues such as limited cache capacity, per-CPU draining, and tight coupling with memcg. This change allows for more scalable and efficient handling of page counters.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 4/7] mm/page_counter: use stock in page_counter_try_charge
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the page_counter_try_charge function to attempt to service a charge request from its stock before attempting to fulfill it through the hierarchy. The patch preserves the existing semantics of stock management, including limiting checks and greedy attempts to refill the stock. It also adds a new function, page_counter_refill_stock, which is used by page_counter_try_charge to refill the stock. No functional changes are intended as no page counters currently enable stock and counter->batch remains at 0.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 5/7] mm/page_counter: introduce an asynchronous drainer
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces an asynchronous drainer for page counters, which iterates through each CPU and flushes any existing charges without affecting unrelated memory cgroups' stock. This approach coalesces duplicate drain requests and improves performance by avoiding unnecessary work on remote CPUs.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 6/7] mm/memcontrol: convert memcg to use page_counter_stock
series_items.patch_summary: This patch converts the memory cgroup (memcg) to use page_counter_stock, which transparently handles stock usage and refills. This change eliminates a special case in try_charge_memcg and removes the 7-memcg cap, allowing each CPU to cache an unbounded number of pages. The patch also enables draining stock on isolated CPUs and addresses a user-visible change for legacy cgroup v1 (memsw). Unused memcg code is removed, preserving obj_stock and FLUSHING_CACHED_CHARGE.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 7/7] mm/memcontrol: add stock to the memsw page_counter
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a separate stock to the memsw page_counter in Linux's memory control system. This change allows memsw (memory swap) to benefit from caching charges, which were previously only applied to memory. The patch also updates various functions to handle the new stock correctly, including allocation and freeing of stocks, charging and uncharging of pages, and handling of hotplug CPU events. As a result, the patch reduces the skew between memory and memsw charges, but still allows for transient drifts due to per-cpu stocks.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series moves the stock management from mem_cgroup to page_counter, allowing each counter to own and drain its own cache. This eliminates the 7 memcg-per-cpu slot limit, random cross-memcg stock drains, and slot traversal. The stock is now a property of the counter rather than the cpu, making it reachable remotely and eliminating the need for synchronous draining. The patch also introduces independent stock management for additional page_counters in each memcg, enabling features like tiered memory limits. The approach taken preserves as much of the old semantics as possible while addressing existing issues with stock management.

This change ensures that folios are not unnecessarily removed from the queue and that their partially mapped status is correctly maintained.

review_comments.raw_body:
On Sat, Aug 29, 2026 at 3:14 AM Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> SWAP_USAGE_OFFLIST_BIT is embedded in the si->inuse_pages usage counter,
> and is meant to sit above any value that counter can reach. However, it
> is defined from BITS_PER_TYPE(atomic_t), so it is bit 30. On a system
> with 4 KiB pages the flag collides with the usage count once that count
> reaches 4 TiB.
>
> swap_usage_in_pages() masks bit 30 out, so whenever the real count has
> that bit set, every caller of it reads 4 TiB low:
>
> * /proc/swaps understates Used by 4 TiB.
>
> * A raw count of exactly 2^30 masks to zero, so try_to_unuse() takes its
>   "if (!swap_usage_in_pages(si)) goto success;" early exit and swapoff
>   tears the device down while pages are still swapped out. Nothing in
>   the rest of swapoff aborts the teardown, so those pages are lost.
>
> Independently of swapoff, the collision also corrupts the counter and
> the plist. On a device in normal use, a free that leaves bit 30 set in
> the count makes swap_usage_sub() see the flag where there is only count,
> and call add_to_avail_list(). It clears the bit with
> fetch_and(~SWAP_USAGE_OFFLIST_BIT), leaving the stored count 4 TiB below
> the real one, and calls plist_add() on a device that is already listed,
> tripping the WARN_ON(!plist_node_empty(node)) in plist_add() and linking
> the node a second time.

> Change the definition of SWAP_USAGE_OFFLIST_BIT to be based on
> atomic_long_t instead. Note that the usage counter field itself is of
> this same type, so it is still a valid bit.

series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds fallback aliases for disabled BMI2 variants in the Zstandard library. When dynamic BMI2 dispatch is disabled, it prevents compilation of BMI2-specific functions and conditionally compiles selectors to avoid naming conflicts. The patch introduces aliases from unavailable BMI2 function names to their default implementations, making the names valid without emitting BMI2-specific code. This change does not modify existing code generation but prepares for future use of these aliases when dynamic BMI2 dispatch is enabled. The goal is to improve flexibility and maintainability by providing a fallback mechanism for disabled BMI2 variants.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/2] zstd: use cpu_feature_enabled() for in-kernel BMI2 dispatch
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the use of BMI2 instructions in the Linux kernel's Zstd compression and decompression code by using the `cpu_feature_enabled()` function to check if the CPU supports BMI2 at boot time, rather than probing CPUID at runtime. This change improves performance by allowing x86 alternatives to resolve feature checks at boot, reducing runtime branches and improving compression and decompression speeds. The patch also keeps the existing HUF conditional layout and makes some minor changes to context structures and accessors.

I do still react to a couple of places. Notably, this part (repeated a
couple of times):

> +#if !defined(ZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES)
>      cctx->bmi2 = ZSTD_cpuSupportsBmi2();
> +#endif

should probably be an "set state" macro the same way ZSTD_USE_BMI2()
is now a "get state" macro.

And:

> +ccflags-$(CONFIG_X86) += -DZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES

We don't have anything like this for any other ZSTD defines, so my gut
feel is that either this is in the wrong place, and it should be in
something like

   lib/zstd/common/zstd_deps.h

which already has kernel-specific stuff in it, or it should just use
#ifdef __KERNEL__ like we use elsewhere for things that are also used
by user space.

The whole situation with ZSTD configuration is a bit strange. I note
that there are things like ZSTD_ARCH_ARM_NEON that the kernel never
uses.

Why is "DYNAMIC_BMI2" a settimg but things like that
ZSTD_ARCH_X86_SSE2 and ZSTD_ARCH_ARM_NEON are never set? This all
looks messy.

Or is there some hidden config I didn't find?

Strange.

             Linus

review_comments.author: Usama Arif
review_comments.summary: Addressed Linus's concerns by adding a 'set state' macro for ZSTD_SET_BMI2() and reorganizing kernel-specific defines.
review_comments.raw_body:
On 31/08/2026 00:06, Linus Torvalds wrote:
> On Sun, 30 Aug 2026 at 15:21, Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev> wrote:
>>
>> Add ZSTD_USE_BMI2() and use it at every runtime BMI2/default selector.
> 
> Thanks, this looks sane to me.
> 
> I do still react to a couple of places. Notably, this part (repeated a
> couple of times):
> 
>> +#if !defined(ZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES)
>>      cctx->bmi2 = ZSTD_cpuSupportsBmi2();
>> +#endif
> 
> should probably be an "set state" macro the same way ZSTD_USE_BMI2()
> is now a "get state" macro.
> 

Ack, have added ZSTD_SET_BMI2():

#if !DYNAMIC_BMI2
#  define ZSTD_USE_BMI2(bmi2) 0
#  define ZSTD_SET_BMI2(state, value) do { } while (0)
#elif defined(ZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES)
#  define ZSTD_USE_BMI2(bmi2) cpu_feature_enabled(X86_FEATURE_BMI2)
#  define ZSTD_SET_BMI2(state, value) do { } while (0)
#else
#  define ZSTD_USE_BMI2(bmi2) (bmi2)
#  define ZSTD_SET_BMI2(state, value) do { (state) = (value); } while (0)
#endif

will use above in next revision.
> And:
> 
>> +ccflags-$(CONFIG_X86) += -DZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES
> 
> We don't have anything like this for any other ZSTD defines, so my gut
> feel is that either this is in the wrong place, and it should be in
> something like
> 
>    lib/zstd/common/zstd_deps.h
> 
> which already has kernel-specific stuff in it, or it should just use
> #ifdef __KERNEL__ like we use elsewhere for things that are also used
> by user space.
> 

Ack, removed it from the Makefile for next revision.

__KERNEL__ alone was insufficient because it is also defined for the x86
compressed boot code. That environment defines __DISABLE_EXPORTS and cannot
use the normal alternatives infrastructure, so it retains zstd\u2019s raw-CPUID
path.

I have added 

#if defined(__KERNEL__) && defined(CONFIG_X86) && \
    !defined(__DISABLE_EXPORTS)
#define ZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES
#endif

in lib/zstd/common/zstd_deps.h for the next revision.


> The whole situation with ZSTD configuration is a bit strange. I note
> that there are things like ZSTD_ARCH_ARM_NEON that the kernel never
> uses.
> 
> Why is "DYNAMIC_BMI2" a settimg but things like that
> ZSTD_ARCH_X86_SSE2 and ZSTD_ARCH_ARM_NEON are never set? This all
> looks messy.
> 

DYNAMIC_BMI2 is defined in lib/zstd/common/portability_macros.h.

ZSTD_ARCH_X86_SSE2 and ZSTD_ARCH_ARM_NEON are upstream zstd configuration
knobs. The kernel import is generated with ZSTD_NO_INTRINSICS [1], so their
automatic definitions are disabled even though some guarded references
remain in the imported source. The kernel cannot use SSE/NEON transparently
because that requires architecture-specific SIMD/FPU state management, whereas
BMI2 operates only on general-purpose registers.

[1] https://github.com/facebook/zstd/blob/dev/contrib/linux-kernel/Makefile#L30

> Or is there some hidden config I didn't find?
> 
> Strange.
> 
>              Linus

series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the ZSTD_initStaticCCtx function to use the ZSTD_cpuSupportsBmi2 helper, which checks for both BMI1 and BMI2 support on x86 CPUs. This ensures that the function behaves correctly even if only one of these instructions is supported. The change has no functional impact on any existing CPU in the field.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/3] zstd: skip the BMI2 probe when dynamic BMI2 dispatch is disabled
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the zstd library to skip the BMI2 probe when dynamic BMI2 dispatch is disabled. This change prevents unnecessary CPUID instructions from being issued, which can be serializing on x86 architectures. The modification adds a conditional check within the ZSTD_cpuSupportsBmi2 function to only perform the probe if DYNAMIC_BMI2 is enabled.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 3/3] zstd: probe the CPU for BMI2 support only once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the ZSTD_cpuSupportsBmi2() function by caching its result instead of probing the CPU for BMI2 support every time it's called. This is done to reduce the overhead of serializing CPUID instructions, which can be expensive especially in busy workloads or under KVM. The cache is stored as a single int with a negative sentinel value and is accessed using READ_ONCE() and WRITE_ONCE() macros to ensure thread safety.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series optimizes the Zstandard (zstd) compression library in the Linux kernel by reducing unnecessary CPUID probes for BMI2 support. The current implementation probes for BMI2 support every time a compression or decompression context is set up, which can lead to performance issues due to serializing CPUID instructions on x86. This patch series introduces caching and dynamic dispatching of BMI2 support, resulting in significant performance improvements (up to 71% reduction in decompression time) by reducing the number of CPUID probes.

Author acknowledged a potential issue with using cpu_feature_enabled(), but expressed uncertainty about its feasibility for standalone library imports and suggested an alternative patch as a better solution.

The author is addressing Eric Biggers' feedback on the patch to probe the CPU for BMI2 support once, not per context. The author agrees that using kernel CPU feature detection is a better approach and has modified the code to use cpu_feature_enabled() in the normal x86 compressor and decompressor objects. review_comments.raw_body:
The only issue I saw with that was that zstd is a standalone library that
is imported, so I am not sure how using cpu_feature_enabled() would work
for the maintainers. If the maintainers are happy with it, I think the
below patch is much better.

---

From: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 05:34:41 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] zstd: use kernel CPU feature detection on x86

Zstd currently probes CPUID while initializing each compression or
decompression context. This bypasses the x86 feature policy used by the
rest of the kernel and repeats a serializing instruction sequence for
every context.

Use cpu_feature_enabled() in the normal x86 compressor and decompressor
objects. Check ABM, BMI1, and BMI2 because the dispatched functions are
compiled with lzcnt, bmi, and bmi2. The checks are alternatives-patched
at boot.

The effect is especially visible under virtualization, where CPUID
normally causes a VM exit. A 4 KiB crypto_acomp benchmark was run in
one-vCPU KVM guests. Comparing the unpatched baseline with this
three-patch series, the median reported ns/op values were:

                         before    after
  compression            16,777   13,635 ns/op  (-18.7%)
  decompression           3,454    1,006 ns/op  (-70.9%)

Keep the existing raw CPUID fallback for preboot and other builds which
cannot use the normal x86 feature infrastructure. Also retain the early
return when dynamic dispatch is disabled.

Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
---
 lib/zstd/Makefile               |  5 +++++
 lib/zstd/common/zstd_internal.h | 18 ++++++++++++++----
 2 files changed, 19 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)

diff --git a/lib/zstd/Makefile b/lib/zstd/Makefile
index be218b5e0ed59..db1d1439f5447 100644
--- a/lib/zstd/Makefile
+++ b/lib/zstd/Makefile
@@ -42,3 +42,8 @@ zstd_common-y := \
 		common/error_private.o \
 		common/fse_decompress.o \
 		common/zstd_common.o \
+
+ifeq ($(CONFIG_X86),y)
+CFLAGS_compress/zstd_compress.o += -DZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES
+CFLAGS_decompress/zstd_decompress.o += -DZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES
+endif
diff --git a/lib/zstd/common/zstd_internal.h b/lib/zstd/common/zstd_internal.h
index 41f190b533209..f7d3bca650747 100644
--- a/lib/zstd/common/zstd_internal.h
+++ b/lib/zstd/common/zstd_internal.h
@@ -31,6 +31,11 @@
 #include "fse.h"
 #include "huf.h"
 #include <linux/xxhash.h>                /* XXH_reset, update, digest */
+
+/* Use the kernel's CPU feature policy in normal x86 kernel builds. */
+#if defined(ZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES)
+#include <asm/cpufeature.h>
+#endif
 #define ZSTD_TRACE 0
 
 /* ---- static assert (debug) --- */
@@ -311,12 +316,17 @@ size_t ZSTD_decodeSeqHeaders(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, int* nbSeqPtr,
  */
 MEM_STATIC int ZSTD_cpuSupportsBmi2(void)
 {
-#if DYNAMIC_BMI2
-    ZSTD_cpuid_t cpuid = ZSTD_cpuid();
-    return ZSTD_cpuid_bmi1(cpuid) && ZSTD_cpuid_bmi2(cpuid);
-#else
+#if !DYNAMIC_BMI2
     /* Nothing looks at the flag in this configuration. */
     return 0;
+#elif defined(ZSTD_USE_KERNEL_CPU_FEATURES)
+    return cpu_feature_enabled(X86_FEATURE_ABM) &&
+           cpu_feature_enabled(X86_FEATURE_BMI1) &&
+           cpu_feature_enabled(X86_FEATURE_BMI2);
+#else
+    ZSTD_cpuid_t cpuid = ZSTD_cpuid();
+    return ZSTD_cpuid_bmi1(cpuid) &&
+           ZSTD_cpuid_bmi2(cpuid);
 #endif
 }
 
--
